clue.text: Old Tommy, in desert, cracked code

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then shuffled

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier stationed in the desert breaks an enemy code.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the old nickname for a British private soldier; the anagram of 'code' sits inside RAT to give REDCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers of earlier centuries wore red tunics, so an old-time Tommy was a redcoat.

clue.text: Still loves needling the barking canine

indicators.note: a needle pierces its way in, so the first pieces are pushed inside the jumbled word
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of the word beside it go crazy

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
still, as in 'still to come', means yet
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O; two of them here

explanation.surface: A dog keeps chewing on someone's affections while barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like a mere article in the surface, but it is the anagram fodder; tennis scores love as O.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye tooth is a canine tooth of the upper jaw, lying under the eye.

clue.text: Soldier material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a non-commissioned army rank

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier material' reads as a recruit with potential, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an army rank above lance corporal; the adjective means relating to the body, physical as opposed to spiritual.

clue.text: Sweet kid has first thing to auction toiletry

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding or dessert

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to have someone on is to kid or tease them
lot one, the first item under the hammer

explanation.surface: A child with a sweet tooth puts a bottle of cologne up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is a verb, to tease. Afters is the British word for dessert, and I is Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave lotion is a scented liquid applied after shaving, a standard toiletry.

clue.text: I'm loving this gas for balloon filling I received from His Majesty

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so the gas sits within the royal word

parts.note: the royal we is what a monarch says in place of I
helium, chemical symbol He, fills party balloons

explanation.surface: A child at a party, delighted with the King's gift of a helium balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'we' is a monarch's way of saying 'I', so 'I' from His Majesty becomes WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Whee is an exclamation of delight or exhilaration, the cry of someone enjoying themselves.

clue.text: Necessity when colossally misconstruing pharmaceutical Euromarket — four times!

definitions.text: Necessity when colossally misconstruing pharmaceutical Euromarket — four times!

parts.note: surface reading: what you need after a huge blunder in reading a drugs market
setter's reading: words meaning harm are confined within four clue words, as the exclamation says

explanation.surface: Some executive has badly misread the European drugs market and must now contain the fallout.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also describes the clue: harm is limited inside four words, as pHARMaceutical, coLOSSally, misconstRUINg and EuroMARket each hold a word for injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage limitation means efforts to reduce the harm after a mistake, which a colossal misjudgement certainly needs.

clue.text: Not ordinarily where to sit to get a tan

definitions.text: Not ordinarily where to sit to get a tan

indicators.note: not in the usual way means the letters are not in their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on an unusual spot to sunbathe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue hints at a place exposed to the elements, where sun and wind will weather your skin, though not where you would usually go.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather station is an outdoor site with instruments recording conditions, exposed to sun all day.

clue.text: Come before hunt for something to eat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to exist or happen earlier than
second meaning: to act as a predator, preying on other animals

explanation.walkthrough: Two words of the same spelling: pre-date, to be earlier, and predate, the back-formation from predator.
explanation.definitionFit: Predating means occurring earlier in time; in zoology predation is the killing of prey for food.

clue.text: One sings a little Elgar, which listener tapes

indicators.note: to tape is to record or bind round, so the pair of words wrap up the single letter

parts.note: which or what, as in 'what book?'
the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: only a small piece of the composer's name is used, its opening

parts.note: the first letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A singer performs a short piece of Elgar, which someone in the audience records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One sings' is a songbird, not a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird of open country, so it is one that sings.

clue.text: Why territories in conflict present a new version of events

definitions.text: present a new version of events

indicators.note: things in conflict are at war and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking why lands at war each tell a different story about the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewrite history is to give a revised, often self-serving, account of past events.

clue.text: Nurse holds stake in occupation

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to nurse is to tend or look after
an ante is a poker player's stake

explanation.surface: A nurse has a financial interest in her own job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' looks like a job, but 'in occupation' means lived in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenanted building has people living in it, so it is in occupation.

clue.text: Officers of the law make county a gift

parts.note: to tip is to give a small gift of money
Staffs is the abbreviation for Staffordshire, a West Midlands county

explanation.surface: Police officers bribe a whole county.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as TIP STAFFS, the answer is an instruction to give Staffordshire a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipstaffs are court officers who make arrests and keep order, named after their staff of office.

clue.text: I'm in Saturday's Telegraph flag flying: page feature, no leader

indicators.note: without its leader means the word loses its front letter

parts.note: a regiment's colours are its flag
up in the air, aloft
p is the abbreviation for page
element, a feature or component, without its opening letter

explanation.surface: A boast from a Saturday paper with its flag flying, about a front-page feature that lacks a lead story.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the answer's own voice: the glossy magazine says where it can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour supplement is the glossy magazine that comes with a weekend newspaper, including Saturday's Telegraph.

clue.text: See 12
See 6
Something taken by Greeks to agorae?

definitions.text: Something taken by Greeks to agorae?

indicators.note: a portion is taken from the following words, so the letters are lifted from inside them

parts.note: the end of one word, the next word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A question about what ancient Greeks carried with them to the marketplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines: a stoa is the sort of thing the Greeks took to their agorae, building them there.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade, typically lining the agora, the public square of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Waits for one who's ordered metal and paper

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
The Times, a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone has ordered supplies of metal and paper and waits for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead times are the delays between placing an order and receiving the goods.

clue.text: With shimmering heat, get buns out?

definitions.text: With shimmering heat, get buns out?

indicators.note: something shimmering wavers and won't hold still, so the letters shift about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a hot day, someone strips off and bares their bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Buns is slang for buttocks; the whole clue describes lying out in hot sun, and 'out' also tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunbathe is to lie exposed to hot sunshine, sometimes with buttocks bared.

clue.text: Notice online artist run through activated red light

indicators.note: something run through something else is driven into its middle

parts.note: a red light is a ban; once it has been given, the thing is banned
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An online notice about an artist who drove through a red light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is not R here: 'run through' is the instruction to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner ad is an advertisement strip across a webpage, a notice seen online.

clue.text: Heads across the London area to collect book

indicators.note: collecting something gathers it in, so the letter goes inside the rest

parts.note: over, as in 'go over the road'
SE is a London postcode district, the south-east
b is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone heads across London to pick up a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' is a noun here, the side of a coin, not a verb of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the face of a coin bearing the head, the side called heads.

clue.text: See 7
Done like poison

parts.note: finished, as in 'time is up'
as, meaning in the way of

explanation.surface: Someone has been finished off with poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done like' reads as killed in the manner of; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javan tree whose sap was used as arrow poison, so the word also names that poison.

clue.text: Groom at stable loft curses engagement

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and arrange, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ban is a curse or anathema

explanation.surface: A stable hand in the hayloft swears about a wedding engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' suggests marriage but means a fight. The battles of St Albans (1455, 1461) opened the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a military engagement, and St Albans saw two such clashes in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: See 4
See 22
We are sent it, specifically for cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the letters round in a loop, so the front letter moves to the back

parts.note: taken as written
i.e., Latin id est, 'that is', used to specify

explanation.surface: Someone has been sent something for a cycling event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like the bike sport; it asks for the first letter of SENTITIE to move round to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: We are beings with separate existence, which is what entities are.

clue.text: Erstwhile City high-flyer?

parts.note: ex means former
EC, the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A former high-flyer from the City of London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An exec, short for executive, is a senior businessperson; high-flyer is a loose example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See 10
Vessels, it's implied, break for the night

parts.note: pots are vessels
the instruction to turn the vessels round is implied by the answer's second half

explanation.surface: Ships put in at port to break their voyage overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split in two, is itself an instruction whose second word turns the first round to give the vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a break in a journey, typically an overnight stay.

clue.text: Maybe Merlot left open for dressing ham? Quite the reverse!

indicators.note: a dressing covers something, so the open word wraps round the wine

parts.note: to undo is to open

indicators.note: going left in an across answer means reading the word backwards

parts.note: Merlot is an example of red wine

explanation.surface: A bottle of Merlot left open to make a dressing for ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' is not meat but a verb: to ham is to overdo things on stage, and 'quite the reverse' asks for the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to overact; the reverse is to underdo, to do too little.
